newsitem.title: UK: S&P may cut East Midlands Elec ratings.
newsitem.headline: S&P may cut East Midlands Elec ratings.

text.p: Standard & Poor's said on Thursday it had placed its AA long-term corporate credit and senior unsecured debt ratings of East Midlands Electricity Plc on CreditWatch with negative implications.
In addition, East Midland's Electricity A1 plus commercial paper rating has also been placed on CreditWatch with negative implications, S&P said in a statement.

The CreditWatch placement follows the announcement by East Midlands Electricity that it is recommending a takeover bid by Dominion Resources Inc (commercial paper rated A2) valuing the company at 1.3 billion stg, S&P said.
"This CreditWatch announcement acknowledges uncertainties concerning the financial implications for East Midlands Electricity if the bid clears the regulatory hurdles," the rating agency said.
"S&P recognises that the funding of such a takeover may lead to weaker debt servicing capacity than would be consistent with its current rating."

"East Midlands Electricity's current ratings reflect the companys's cash-generative core business, a stable regulatory environment, and a relatively strong financial profile. Its primary bisiness is the monopoly distribution of electricity within its service area, which is expected to outperform the UK average over the medium term," S&P said.
Going forward, S&P said it would review the credit implications of a successful bid for East Midlands Electricity.
S&P said it would assess the following
-- Any regulatory or governmental actions that may have implications for the proposed takeover.
-- The effects on the financial profile of East Midlands Electricity of the acquisition.
-- The group structure and the location of the debt financing within that structure, and
-- Any operational benefits that may arise from the takeover.
"Following an assessment of these and other factors, S&P will adjust the current long-term rating as appropriate," the rating agency said.
